stories.title: Ukrainians blame authorities for storing ammunition in residential areas — media
stories.summary: International human rights organizations earlier reported that Ukrainian authorities use kindergartens and residential buildings to deploy military equipment
article_sentences: Ukrainian residents are angry that the country’s authorities have set up ammunition depots in residential areas, The Guardian reported.
"Those who set up the depot here are to blame.
There are people here, this is a village.
You can’t keep something like that here," a resident of the Kiev Region told the newspaper.
International human rights organizations had earlier reported that Ukrainian authorities use kindergartens and residential buildings to deploy military equipment.

stories.title: Freed Hongkonger sent back to jail as storm delays deportation from Philippines
stories.summary: A Hong Kong man has been returned to a Philippine prison in what his legal team condemned as “illegal detention”, after severe weather halted his deportation following his release. Tang Lung-wai’s Philippine lawyer, Blessie Rose Carpena, told the South China Morning Post that prison authorities escorted Tang to the Bureau of Immigration last Friday. However, because government offices were suspended due to a passing typhoon, he was returned to the maximum-security New Bilibid Prison in...

stories.title: Malaysia’s Sarawak eyes cloud seeding as haze worsens
stories.summary: The cloud-seeding also aims to replenish critically depleted reservoirs and dams after a prolonged dry spell.
article_sentences: Malaysia’s Sarawak state is planning cloud seeding operations in early September, officials said on Aug 31, as smoke from fires in neighbouring Indonesia pushes air quality to hazardous levels.

Indonesia, a vast archipelago, has for weeks battled wildfires that have led to school closures and thousands of people requiring medical treatment, with smoke also drifting across to Malaysia and Singapore.
Sarawak, which shares a border with Indonesia’s Kalimantan province on Borneo island, has been the most affected by the haze.
Sarawak Disaster Management Committee chairman Douglas Uggah Embas said on Aug 31 that cloud seeding could be carried out between Sept 3 and 5, if weather and atmospheric conditions permit.
“Cloud seeding can be carried out only when suitable cloud formations and atmospheric conditions are present – it cannot create rain in the absence of suitable clouds,” Uggah told reporters.
Air quality deteriorated sharply across Sarawak on Aug 31, with seven locations recording hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 300, led by Serian district at 475.
Under national guidelines, API readings above 300 are considered hazardous, while levels exceeding 500 trigger consideration of a local emergency.
“If an emergency is declared, it will strictly be enforced within that specific locality, not for the entire state,” Uggah said.
The cloud-seeding also aims to replenish critically depleted reservoirs and dams after a prolonged dry spell.
State satellite monitoring detected nine active hot spots in Sarawak, compared with 1,180 in Indonesia’s Kalimantan region.
Kalimantan recorded 15,587 hot spots between January and late August, including more than 13,000 in August alone.

“This issue is a diplomatic issue,” Uggah said, adding that the state authorities had urged the federal government to raise the matter with Jakarta under the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution.
